candidates.name: Intisar A/103–Brega Gas Pipeline
aka: Gas Transfer Project 103 Intisar Field to a Coastal Network
candidates.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC), via Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company and Zueitina Oil Company (Waha Oil Company system)
candidates.to: Brega gas distribution network / coastal grid

evidence.note: NOC begins first phase (~30 km) linking Field 103 in the Farigh system to a reception point in the Zueitina area, injecting into an existing 42-inch pipeline operated by Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company, supplying Brega and the coastal network. Reported March 17, citing a March 15 Libya Observer report.

Corroborates: Farigh field (Zueitina axis, Field 103A) tied to 42-inch trunkline at km 91 in the Sirte network, first-phase 30 km segment delivering gas to Brega, launched March 20, 2026; operator Waha Oil Company (NOC/TotalEnergies/ConocoPhillips).
Libya Observer's own report naming the project the 'Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline', first phase now pumping gas.

NOC began testing the full line April 13, 2026: a 42-inch, ~130 km pipeline connecting the Intisar A/103 gas field to the Brega distribution network, designed to recover ~150 MMcf/d of previously-flared gas; stalled for 16+ years before this recent completion; commissioning by Sirte Oil Company and Zueitina Oil Company teams.
Corroborates the 130 km / 42-inch Intisar A/103-to-Brega pipeline trial, 150 MMcf/d flared-gas recovery target, and the 16-year stall.
Libya Observer in-brief on the same trial-operation milestone, described as a 'strategic gas pipeline'.
Independent corroboration of the March first-phase Farigh-Brega launch, same specs (30 km, Zueitina axis Field 103A to km-91 trunkline).

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster line matches this Zueitina/Field-103-to-Brega corridor by name. However the 42-inch diameter and Brega destination are identical to P1856 'Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline' (Intesar Oil field->Mersa Brega, status=operating, len=333.0, dia=42.00, cap=42.48) already in the roster — the consolidator should check whether this is (a) a genuinely separate/parallel 130 km line feeding the same corridor (Zueitina's own project page calls it 'Gas Transfer Project 103 Intisar Field to a Coastal Network', distinct from Waha's Intesar-Brega trunk), or (b) the same physical asset as P1856 whose 'operating' status is stale/premature given that press describes it as stalled 16 years and only entering trial commissioning in April 2026. Either way it is not cleanly represented by the current P1856 record as-is.
